page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Faint marks in the left margin (small strokes beside lines 8, 11 and 19) are not printed text and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: dummodò in Domino. Argumentum ducit à contrarijs. Nam si ad vitam mariti alligata est mulier, morte ergo soluitur: postquam soluta est, nubat cui velit. Hoc (cui velit) quadrat de viduis, de virginibus non item: Nam illæ sunt adhuc in potestate maiorum. Ambrosius eò refert, ut intelligamus coactas damnari nuptias. Quia (inquit) inuitæ nuptiæ solent malos proventus habere. His ergo verbis apertissimè fecundas nuptias approbat Apostolus aduersus eorum tyrannidem, qui vetuerunt illis interesse clericos. Idem[?] etiam facit, I.Tim. 5. cum inquit, Volo viduas iuniores nubere, &c. Vetus testamentum fecundas nuptias legitimas, altero coniuge mortuo, etiam non damnat, sed approbat. Nam Abrahamus aliam duxit uxorem, nomine Cethuram, Gen.25. & Abigail, Nabal mortuo, nupsit Dauidi, I.Reg.25. De nuptijs non solum fecundis, sed etiam tertijs & pluribus, idem sentiunt Ambrosius in cap. 3. Epist. ad Tim. Epiphanius lib. 2. Tom. 1. Hæresi 59. Hieronymus in Epist. ad Marcellinum: & pro libris aduersus Iouianū. Lombardus lib. 4 Dist. 42. Sed quid est, quod ad dit, Modò in Domino? Hoc quidam intelligunt de coniugio pari, ubi fit utrinque religio eadem, hoc est, ut maritus incredula uxore liberatus, fidelem ducat, & uxor fidelis, ex experta prius, quifit[?] impio nexam esse, abhorreat ab impijs: pio vero nubat viro: q.d. Paulus: Modo fit Christianum coniugium, hoc est,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "dummodò" accent; "Idem" split across the line break at "clericos." (I and dem on separate lines, so [?] is placed on the whole word); "ad dit," as printed, possibly "addit" divided without a hyphen; "quifit" where the letter after "qui" is unclear; "experta" and "uxore" are split at line ends with no printed hyphen, so written whole. Hyphens kept where printed: tyranni-, nu-, er-, ap-, alliga-, Lom-, reli-, Pau-, intelli-, ty-, abhor- (abhorreat written whole). Page furniture: running head "CONCIONES" and page number 316 as printed; no catchword or signature. Marginal marks are not text, so no notes are transcribed.
